nodes.statement: {\hat{\Gamma}}({q}_0')  \le 125339 \times \left( \frac{d-2}{f(d-1)-f(1)} \right)^2  d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right)

nodes.name: Equation (136)
nodes.statement: {\hat{\Gamma}}({q}_0'') \le \frac{266.45}{(f(1)-f(0))^2} d \log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon} \right)

nodes.name: Equation (137)
nodes.statement: {\hat{\Gamma}}({q}_0''') \le \frac{266.45}{(f(d)-f(d-1))^2} d \log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon} \right)

nodes.name: Equation (139)
nodes.statement:
{\hat{\Gamma}} ({q}_0) &\le \min \Bigg\{ 125339\times \left( \frac{d-2}{f(d-1)-f(1)} \right)^2 d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right) , \frac{266.45}{(f(1)-f(0))^2} d \log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon} \right) ,\notag \\
    &   \kern23em\frac{266.45}{(f(d)-f(d-1))^2} d \log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon} \right) \Bigg\} \notag\\
    &\le 125339 \times \min \left\{\frac{(d-2)^2}{(f(d-1)-f(1))^2}, \frac{1}{(f(1)-f(0))^2} , \frac{1}{(f(d)-f(d-1))^2}  \right\} \times d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right) \notag\\
    &\leq 376017 \times \frac{d^2}{(f(d)-f(0))^2}  d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right) \notag\\
    &= { 376017 \times \frac{1}{{\beta}^2} \left( \frac{{U}-{L}}{f({U})-f({L})} \right)^2 d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right)}

nodes.name: Conclusion
Equation (140)
nodes.statement: {\hat{\Gamma}} ({q}_0) \leq 376017 {H(f)} d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right)

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5
nodes.statement_short: From Lemma 12, remove the factor $\frac{(d-L')U'}{(d-U')L'}$: directly if $\alpha=(U'-L')/2$, else by subdividing $[L',U']$ (Lemmas 13-15).

nodes.name: Lemma 12
Preliminary bound on Gamma-hat with an extra factor
nodes.statement:
Let $d\geq 3$. For any ${L}',{U}' \in \{1 ,\dots, d-1\}$ with ${L}' < {U}'$ and $f({L}')<f({U}')$, there exists ${q}_0 \in \left(\frac {{L}'} {d}, \frac {{U}'} {d}\right)$ such that ${\hat{\Gamma}} ({q}_0) $ defined in \eqref{eq:def:fTp} satisfies 
\begin{equation} {\hat{\Gamma}} ({q}_0)  \leq 1253.39 \times \frac{ (d-{L}') {U}' }{{\alpha}^2 (d-{U}'){L}'} \left( \frac{{U}'-{L}'}{f({U}')-f({L}')} \right)^2  d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right),
\end{equation} 

where ${\alpha} := \frac{1}{2} \min\left\{{U}'-{L}',\sqrt{{L}'},\sqrt{d-{U}'}\right\}$.
nodes.label: lem:existence_pre

nodes.name: Equation (141)
nodes.statement: {\hat{\Gamma}} ({q}_0)  \leq 1253.39 \times \frac{ (d-{L}') {U}' }{{\alpha}^2 (d-{U}'){L}'} \left( \frac{{U}'-{L}'}{f({U}')-f({L}')} \right)^2  d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right),
nodes.label: eq:existence_pre

nodes.name: Pointer to the proof of Lemma 12
nodes.statement: See Appendix \ref{proof:lem:existence_pre}.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: Comparing Proposition \ref{prop:existence} and Lemma \ref{lem:existence_pre}, we see that the main difference is the $\frac{ (d-{L}') {U}' }{(d-{U}'){L}'}$ term. In the remainder of the proof, we manage to eliminate the $\frac{ (d-{L}') {U}' }{(d-{U}'){L}'}$ term from \eqref{eq:existence_pre}. Since ${\alpha} = \frac{1}{2} \min\left\{{U}'-{L}',\sqrt{{L}'},\sqrt{d-{U}'}\right\}$, we consider the following two cases.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to removing the extra factor; two cases on $\alpha$.

nodes.name: Case i
nodes.statement_short: Case i: the factor is at most 25.

nodes.name: Equation (142)
nodes.statement: {U}'-{L}' \leq \min\left\{ \sqrt{{L}'} , \sqrt{d-{U}'} \right\}.

nodes.name: Case ii
nodes.statement_short: Case ii: subdivide into intervals and apply Lemma 12 on the steepest one.

nodes.name: Subdivision
Equation (144)
nodes.statement: {\alpha} = \frac{1}{2} \min\left\{ \sqrt{{L}'} , \sqrt{d-{U}'}\right \} < \frac{{U}'-{L}'}{2}.
nodes.label: eq:case2:alpha

nodes.name: Equation (145)
nodes.statement: {\tau} &:= \left\lfloor \frac{{U}'-{L}'}{\lceil 2{{\alpha}} \rceil} \right\rfloor,

nodes.name: Equation (146)
nodes.statement: {{\lambda}_{{i}}} &:= {L}' + {i}\cdot\lceil 2{{\alpha}} \rceil    \text { for } {i} = 0,\cdots, {\tau}-1,
nodes.label: eq:def:sigma

nodes.name: Equation (148)
nodes.statement: {{{\alpha}}_{{i}}} := \frac{1}{2} \min\left\{ {{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}-{{\lambda}_{{i}}} , \sqrt{{{\lambda}_{{i}}}} , \sqrt{d-{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}}\right \}  \text { for }  {i} = 0,  \cdots , {\tau}-1.
nodes.label: eq:def:alpha:i

nodes.name: Lemma 13
alpha_i at least alpha
nodes.statement: ${{{\alpha}}_{{i}}} \ge {{\alpha}}$ for all ${i} \in \{0,\cdots, {\tau}-1\}$.
nodes.label: lem:exi:alp

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 13
nodes.statement_short: Each of the three terms in $\alpha_i$ is at least $\alpha$, using $L'\le\lambda_i<\lambda_{i+1}\le U'$ and the choice of spacing.

nodes.name: Root terms
Equation (150)
nodes.statement: \frac{1}{2} \min\left\{ \sqrt{{{\lambda}_{{i}}}} , \sqrt{d-{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}} \right\} \ge \frac{1}{2} \min\left\{ \sqrt{{L}'} , \sqrt{d-{U}'}\right \} = {{\alpha}}.
nodes.label: eq:aphi:second-thrid

nodes.name: Length terms
Equation (151)
nodes.statement: \frac{{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}-{{\lambda}_{{i}}}}{2} = \frac{\lceil2{{\alpha}}\rceil}{2} \ge {{\alpha}};
nodes.label: eq:aphi:first:tau-1

nodes.name: Equation (152)
nodes.statement: \frac{{{\lambda}_{{\tau}}}-{{\lambda}_{{\tau}-1}}}{2} = \frac{{U}'-{L}'-({\tau}-1)\lceil2{{\alpha}}\rceil}{2} \ge \frac{{U}'-{L}' - \left( \frac{{U}'-{L}'}{\lceil2{{\alpha}}\rceil}-1 \right) \lceil2{{\alpha}}\rceil}{2} = \frac{\lceil2{{\alpha}}\rceil}{2} \ge {{\alpha}}.
nodes.label: eq:aphi:first:tau

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: Combining the above three inequalities, along with the definition of ${{{\alpha}}_{{i}}}$ in \eqref{eq:def:alpha:i}, yields the desired result.

nodes.name: Lemmas 14 and 15
Bounded ratio on subintervals
nodes.statement: $\frac{(d-{{\lambda}_{{i}}}){{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}}{(d-{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}){{\lambda}_{{i}}}} \le 25$ for any ${i} = 0,\cdots, {\tau}-1$.
nodes.label: lem:exi:alp_dif

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 14
nodes.statement_short: Each subinterval has length at most $4\min\{\sqrt{\lambda_i},\sqrt{d-\lambda_{i+1}}\}$, giving a ratio at most $5\times5$.

nodes.name: Lengths
Equation (153)
nodes.statement: {{\lambda}_{{i}+1}} - {{\lambda}_{{i}}} = \lceil 2{{\alpha}} \rceil \leq 4{{\alpha}}+2;

nodes.name: Equation (154)
nodes.statement:
{{\lambda}_{{\tau}}}-{{\lambda}_{{\tau}-1}} &= {U}' - ({L}'+({\tau}-1)\lceil2{{\alpha}}\rceil) \notag\\ 
    &= {U}' - {L}' - \left( \left\lfloor \frac{{U}'-{L}'}{\lceil2{{\alpha}}\rceil} \right\rfloor - 1 \right) \lceil 2{{\alpha}} \rceil \notag\\ 
    &< {U}' - {L}' - \left( \frac{{U}'-{L}'}{\lceil2{{\alpha}}\rceil} - 2 \right) \lceil 2{{\alpha}} \rceil \notag\\ 
    &= 2 \lceil 2{{\alpha}} \rceil \notag\\ 
    &\leq 4{{\alpha}} + 2.

nodes.name: Relative lengths
nodes.statement:
It then follows that for all $ {i} = 0,\cdots,{\tau}-1$,
\begin{align}
    {{\lambda}_{{i}+1}} - {{\lambda}_{{i}}} &\leq 4{{\alpha}} + 2 \notag\\ 
    &= 2 \min\{\sqrt{{L}'} , \sqrt{d-{U}'}\} + 2 \notag\\ 
    &\le 4 \min\{\sqrt{{L}'} , \sqrt{d-{U}'}\} \notag\\ 
    &\le 4 \min\{\sqrt{{{\lambda}_{{i}}}} , \sqrt{d-{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}}\},
\end{align}
where the equality follows from \eqref{eq:case2:alpha}; the second inequality follows from the assumption that $ 1 \le {L}' < {U}' \le d-1$; the last inequality follows from \eqref{eq:sigi:lu}.

nodes.name: Equation (155)
nodes.statement:
{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}} - {{\lambda}_{{i}}} &\leq 4{{\alpha}} + 2 \notag\\ 
    &= 2 \min\{\sqrt{{L}'} , \sqrt{d-{U}'}\} + 2 \notag\\ 
    &\le 4 \min\{\sqrt{{L}'} , \sqrt{d-{U}'}\} \notag\\ 
    &\le 4 \min\{\sqrt{{{\lambda}_{{i}}}} , \sqrt{d-{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}}\},

nodes.name: Conclusion
Equation (156)
nodes.statement: \frac{(d-{{\lambda}_{{i}}}){{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}}{(d-{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}){{\lambda}_{{i}}}} \leq \frac{(d-{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}+4\sqrt{d-{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}}) ({{\lambda}_{{i}}}+4\sqrt{{{\lambda}_{{i}}}})}{(d-{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}){{\lambda}_{{i}}}}=  \frac{(\sqrt{d-{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}}+4)}{\sqrt{d-{{\lambda}_{{i}+1}}}}\cdot\frac {(\sqrt{{{\lambda}_{{i}}}}+4)}{\sqrt{{{\lambda}_{{i}}}}}\le 5\times 5=25,

nodes.name: A subinterval at least as steep as the whole interval
nodes.statement: $\exists {\ell} \in \{ 0,\cdots,{\tau}-1 \}$ such that $\frac{f({{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}})-f({{\lambda}_{{\ell}}})}{{{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}}-{{\lambda}_{{\ell}}}} \ge \frac{f({U}')-f({L}')}{{U}'-{L}'}$.
nodes.label: lem:exi:slp

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 15
nodes.statement_short: If every subinterval were less steep, summing the increments would give $f(U')-f(L')<f(U')-f(L')$.

nodes.name: Assume contrary
nodes.statement_short: Assume every subinterval has a smaller slope.

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement_short: Sum the increments to reach a contradiction.

nodes.name: Finish Case ii
nodes.statement:
We are now ready to finish the proof of Case ii) using the above results. Upon applying Lemma \ref{lem:existence_pre} with ${L}' = {{\lambda}_{{\ell}}}$ and ${U}' = {{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}}$ as defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:exi:slp}, we have that
$\exists {q}_0 \in \left(\frac{{{\lambda}_{{\ell}}}}{d} , \frac{{{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}}}{d}\right) $    such that 
\begin{align} 
{\hat{\Gamma}} ({q}_0)  &\leq 1253.39 \times \frac{(d-{{\lambda}_{{\ell}}} ) {{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}} }{{{{\alpha}}_{{\ell}}}^2 (d-{{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}}){{\lambda}_{{\ell}}}} \left( \frac{{{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}}-{{\lambda}_{{\ell}}}}{f({{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}})-f({{\lambda}_{{\ell}}})} \right)^2  d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right) \notag\\ 
&\le 31334.75 \times \frac{1}{{{{\alpha}}_{{\ell}}}^2} \left( \frac{{{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}}-{{\lambda}_{{\ell}}}}{f({{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}})-f({{\lambda}_{{\ell}}})} \right)^2  d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right) \notag\\ 
&\le 31334.75 \times \frac{1}{{{{\alpha}}_{{\ell}}}^2} \left( \frac{{U}'-{L}'}{f({U}')-f({L}')} \right)^2  d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right) \notag\\ 
&\le 31334.75 \times \frac{1}{{{\alpha}}^2} \left( \frac{{U}'-{L}'}{f({U}')-f({L}')} \right)^2  d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right)  
\end{align} 
where the second inequality follows from Lemma  \ref{lem:exi:alp_dif}; the third inequality follows from Lemma \ref{lem:exi:slp}; the last inequality follows from Lemma \ref{lem:exi:alp}. 
This completes the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:existence}.

nodes.name: Equation (159)
nodes.statement:
{\hat{\Gamma}} ({q}_0)  &\leq 1253.39 \times \frac{(d-{{\lambda}_{{\ell}}} ) {{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}} }{{{{\alpha}}_{{\ell}}}^2 (d-{{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}}){{\lambda}_{{\ell}}}} \left( \frac{{{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}}-{{\lambda}_{{\ell}}}}{f({{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}})-f({{\lambda}_{{\ell}}})} \right)^2  d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right) \notag\\ 
&\le 31334.75 \times \frac{1}{{{{\alpha}}_{{\ell}}}^2} \left( \frac{{{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}}-{{\lambda}_{{\ell}}}}{f({{\lambda}_{{\ell}+1}})-f({{\lambda}_{{\ell}}})} \right)^2  d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right) \notag\\ 
&\le 31334.75 \times \frac{1}{{{{\alpha}}_{{\ell}}}^2} \left( \frac{{U}'-{L}'}{f({U}')-f({L}')} \right)^2  d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right) \notag\\ 
&\le 31334.75 \times \frac{1}{{{\alpha}}^2} \left( \frac{{U}'-{L}'}{f({U}')-f({L}')} \right)^2  d\log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon } \right)

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 12
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound $\int_{L'/d}^{U'/d}\Delta(q)dq$ with the saddle-point bound (Lemma 18) and Stirling (Lemma 16), then apply the mean value theorem to get $q_0$.

nodes.name: Preliminary lemmas
Stirling-type bounds on binomial terms
nodes.label: lem:stirling

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 16
nodes.statement_short: Substitute Stirling's upper and lower bounds for the factorials.

nodes.name: Stirling
Stirling's approximation
nodes.statement:
\begin{equation} \sqrt{2\pi} \, n^{n+\frac{1}{2}} \, e^{-n} \le n! \le e \, n^{n+\frac{1}{2}} \, e^{-n}.
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Lower bound
Upper bound
nodes.statement:
Similarly, we also have
\begin{align*}
\binom{d}{j} \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j} &= \frac{d!}{j!(d-j)!} \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j} \\ 
&\le \frac{e d^{d+1/2} e^{-d}}{\sqrt{2\pi} j^{j+1/2} e^{-j} \sqrt{2\pi} (d-j)^{d-j+1/2} e^{-d+j}} \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j} \\ 
&= \frac{e}{2\pi} \sqrt{\frac{d}{j(d-j)}}.
\end{align*}
Combining the two bounds gives the desired result.

nodes.name: Saddle-point lower bounds on Beta-type integrals
assumptions: For any $j >  i  > 0$ and $d > j +  i  $
nodes.label: lem:int_j_alpha

nodes.name: Equation (161)
nodes.statement: \int_{\frac {j}{d}}^{\frac {j+ i }{d}} {q}^j (1-{q})^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} {q} &\geq \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j} \frac{j(d-j- i )}{ i  d^2} \left( 1 - \exp\left( \frac{-i ^2 d  }{j (d-j- i )} \right) \right),
nodes.label: eq:lem3_1

nodes.name: Equation (162)
nodes.statement: \int_{\frac {j- i }{d}}^{\frac {j}{d}} {q}^j (1-{q})^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} {q} &\geq \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j} \frac{(j- i )(d-j)}{i d^2 } \left( 1 - \exp\left( \frac{- i ^2 d }{(j- i )(d-j)} \right) \right).
nodes.label: eq:lem3_2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 17
nodes.statement_short: Write the integrand as $\exp(\varphi(t)-\varphi(0))$ and lower-bound $\varphi$ by a linear function via its derivative.

nodes.name: First inequality
Define varphi
Equation (163)
nodes.statement: {\varphi}(x) := j\ln(j+xd)+(d-j)\ln(d-j-xd), \quad x \in \left[-\frac { i }{d},\frac { i }{d}\right].
nodes.label: eq:def:varphi(x)

nodes.name: Derivative bound
nodes.statement_short: Derivative bound gives a linear lower bound on $\varphi(t)-\varphi(0)$.

nodes.name: Equation (164)
nodes.statement: {\varphi}({t})-{\varphi}(0) = \int_0^{t} {\varphi}^\prime (x) {\,\mathrm{d}} x \geq \int_0^{t} \frac{- i d^2 }{j(d-j- i )} {\,\mathrm{d}} x = \frac{-  i d^2}{j(d-j- i )} {t},\; \forall{t} \in \left[0,\frac  i  d\right].
nodes.label: eq:lb:varphi(t)-varphi(0)

nodes.name: Integrate
nodes.statement:
By the definition of ${\varphi}$ in \eqref{eq:def:varphi(x)}, we have
\begin{align} {\varphi}({t})-{\varphi}(0)=\ln\left( \left( \frac{j+{t} d}{j} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j-{t} d}{d-j} \right)^{d-j}\right),\;\forall  {t} \in \left[-\frac  i  d,\frac  i  d\right].
\end{align}
It follows that 
\begin{align*}
\int_{\frac {j}{d}}^{\frac {j+ i }{d}} {q}^j (1-{q})^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} {q} &= \int_0^{\frac { i } {d}} \left( \frac{j+{t} d}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j-{t} d}{d} \right)^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} {t} \\ 
&= \int_0^{\frac { i } {d}} \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j}  \left( \frac{j+{t} d}{j} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j-{t} d}{d-j} \right)^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} {t} \\ 
&= \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j}  \int_0^{\frac { i } {d}} \exp({\varphi}({t}) - {\varphi}(0)) {\,\mathrm{d}} {t} \\ 
&\ge \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j}  \int_0^{\frac { i } {d}} \exp\left(\frac{- i d^2 }{j(d-j- i )} {t}\right) {\,\mathrm{d}} {t} \\ 
&= \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j} \frac{j(d-j- i )}{ i d^2} \left( 1 - \exp\left( \frac{- i ^2 d }{j (d-j- i )} \right) \right),
\end{align*}
where the first line follows by setting $q$ to equal $t+\frac{j}{d}$ for some $t$; the third line follows from \eqref{eq:varphi(t)-varphi(0)}; the fourth line follows from \eqref{eq:lb:varphi(t)-varphi(0)}.

This proves the desired inequality~\eqref{eq:lem3_1}.

nodes.name: Equation (165)
nodes.statement: {\varphi}({t})-{\varphi}(0)=\ln\left( \left( \frac{j+{t} d}{j} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j-{t} d}{d-j} \right)^{d-j}\right),\;\forall  {t} \in \left[-\frac  i  d,\frac  i  d\right].
nodes.label: eq:varphi(t)-varphi(0)

nodes.name: Second inequality
Derivative bound
Integrate
nodes.statement:
Then we can deduce that 
\begin{align*}
\int_{\frac {j- i }{d} }^{\frac j d} {q}^j (1-{q})^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} {q} &= \int_{-\frac { i } {d}}^0 \left( \frac{j+{t} d}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j-{t} d}{d} \right)^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} {t} \\ 
&= \int_{-\frac { i } {d}}^0 \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j}  \left( \frac{j+{t} d}{j} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j-{t} d}{d-j} \right)^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} {t} \\ 
&= \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j}  \int_{-\frac { i } {d}}^0 \exp({\varphi}({t}) - {\varphi}(0)) {\,\mathrm{d}} {t} \\ 
&\ge \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j}  \int_{-\frac { i } {d}}^0 \exp\left(\frac{ id^2  }{(j- i )(d-j)} {t}\right) {\,\mathrm{d}} {t} \\ 
&= \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j} \frac{(j- i )(d-j)}{ i d^2 } \left( 1 - \exp\left( \frac{-  i ^2 d}{(j- i )(d-j)} \right) \right),
\end{align*}
which establishes the inequality~\eqref{eq:lem3_2}.

nodes.name: Lower bound on the integral over [L'/d, U'/d]
nodes.label: lem:int_U_L

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 18
nodes.statement_short: Split on whether $j$ is in the lower or upper half of $[L',U']$; apply Lemma 17 with $i=\alpha$ and $1-e^{-x}\ge x(2-x)/2$.

nodes.name: Split
nodes.statement: We split the proof into the following two cases, depending on whether $j$ is in the range $j\in \left[{L}',\frac {{L}'+{U}'} {2} \right]$, or in the range $j\in \left(\frac {{L}'+{U}'} {2} ,{U}'\right]$.
nodes.statement_short: Two cases on the position of $j$.

nodes.name: Case i
Apply Lemma 17
nodes.statement:
Case i): ${L}' \le j \le \frac{{U}'+{L}'}{2}$. It follows that $j+{\alpha}\leq {U}'<d$ since ${\alpha}\leq \frac{{U}'-{L}'}{2}$ by definition. We also have $j>{\alpha}>0$ since ${L}'>{\alpha}$ by definition. Thus $j,d,i={\alpha}$ satisfy the premise of Lemma~\ref{lem:int_j_alpha}. Using the inequality~\eqref{eq:lem3_1} with $i={\alpha}$, we obtain 
\begin{align} \int_{\frac {{L}'}{d}}^{\frac {{U}'}{d}} {q}^j (1-{q})^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} {q} &\ge \int_{\frac j d}^{\frac {j+{\alpha}}{d}} {q}^j (1-{q})^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} {q} \notag \\
&\ge \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j} \frac{j(d-j-{\alpha})}{{\alpha} d^2} \left( 1 - \exp\left( \frac{-{\alpha}^2 d }{j (d-j-{\alpha})} \right) \right).
\end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (166)
nodes.statement:
\int_{\frac {{L}'}{d}}^{\frac {{U}'}{d}} {q}^j (1-{q})^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} {q} &\ge \int_{\frac j d}^{\frac {j+{\alpha}}{d}} {q}^j (1-{q})^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} {q} \notag \\
&\ge \left( \frac{j}{d} \right)^j \left( \frac{d-j}{d} \right)^{d-j} \frac{j(d-j-{\alpha})}{{\alpha} d^2} \left( 1 - \exp\left( \frac{-{\alpha}^2 d }{j (d-j-{\alpha})} \right) \right).
nodes.label: eq:upint:1b1

nodes.name: Exponential bound
nodes.statement:
Using the fact that  
\begin{align} 1-e^{-x} \geq \frac{1}{2} x(2-x),\;\forall x\ge 0,
\end{align} 
we have 
\begin{align} \frac{j(d-j-{\alpha})}{{\alpha} d^2} \left( 1 - \exp\left( \frac{- {\alpha}^2 d }{j (d-j-{\alpha})} \right) \right) &\ge \frac{j(d-j-{\alpha})}{{\alpha} d^2} \times \frac{1}{2} \frac{{\alpha}^2 d}{j(d-j-{\alpha})} \left(2 - \frac{{\alpha}^2 d}{j(d-j-{\alpha})}\right) \notag\\ 
&= \frac{{\alpha}}{2d} \left(2 - \frac{ {\alpha}^2 d}{j(d-j-{\alpha})}\right).
\end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (167)
nodes.statement: 1-e^{-x} \geq \frac{1}{2} x(2-x),\;\forall x\ge 0,
nodes.label: eq:1-e-x:bound

nodes.name: Equation (168)
nodes.statement:
\frac{j(d-j-{\alpha})}{{\alpha} d^2} \left( 1 - \exp\left( \frac{- {\alpha}^2 d }{j (d-j-{\alpha})} \right) \right) &\ge \frac{j(d-j-{\alpha})}{{\alpha} d^2} \times \frac{1}{2} \frac{{\alpha}^2 d}{j(d-j-{\alpha})} \left(2 - \frac{{\alpha}^2 d}{j(d-j-{\alpha})}\right) \notag\\ 
&= \frac{{\alpha}}{2d} \left(2 - \frac{ {\alpha}^2 d}{j(d-j-{\alpha})}\right).
nodes.label: eq:upint:1b2

nodes.name: Correction term
nodes.statement_short: Show the correction term is at most 1 in two sub-cases.

nodes.name: Sub-cases
nodes.statement: Next, we argue that $\frac{{\alpha}^2 d}{j(d-j-{\alpha})}\leq 1$. This is done by dividing into the following two sub-cases:

nodes.name: Sub-case j<d/2
Sub-case j>=d/2
Conclude Case i
Case ii
Apply Lemma 17
Exponential bound
Correction term
nodes.statement_short: Correction term at most 1 in two sub-cases.

nodes.name: Integral bound
nodes.statement:
Using the above results, we are now in a position to prove Lemma \ref{lem:existence_pre}.
Recalling from \eqref{eq:convert_delta} that
\begin{equation*}
{\Delta({q})} = \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {q}^j (1-{q})^{d-j} (f(j+1) - f(j)).
\end{equation*}
Note that ${\Delta({q})}$ is continuous w.r.t. ${q}$. Assuming ${L}', {U}' \in\{1,\dots, d-1\}$ with $ {L}'<{U}'$ and $f({L}')<f({U}')$, we can calculate the integral of ${\Delta({q})}$ for ${q} \in \left[ \frac{{L}'}{d} , \frac{{U}'}{d} \right]$ as follows:
\begin{align}
\int_{\frac{{L}'}{d}}^{\frac{{U}'}{d}} {\Delta({q})} {\,\mathrm{d}} q &= \int_{\frac{{L}'}{d}}^{\frac{{U}'}{d}} \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {q}^j (1-{q})^{d-j} (f(j+1) - f(j)) {\,\mathrm{d}} q \notag\\ 
&\ge \int_{\frac{{L}'}{d}}^{\frac{{U}'}{d}} \sum\limits_{j={L}'}^{{U}'-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {q}^j (1-{q})^{d-j} (f(j+1) - f(j)) {\,\mathrm{d}} q \notag\\
&= \sum\limits_{j={L}'}^{{U}'-1} \frac{d-j}{d} \binom{d}{j} (f(j+1)-f(j)) \int_{\frac{{L}'}{d}}^{\frac{{U}'}{d}} {q}^j (1-{q})^{d-j} {\,\mathrm{d}} q \notag\\ 
&\ge \sum\limits_{j={L}'}^{{U}'-1} \frac{d-j}{d} \binom{d}{j} (f(j+1)-f(j)) \left(\frac{j}{d}\right)^j \left(\frac{d-j}{d}\right)^{d-j} \frac{{\alpha}}{2d} \\ 
&\ge \sum\limits_{j={L}'}^{{U}'-1} \frac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{e^2} \sqrt{\frac{d}{j(d-j)}} \frac{d-j}{d} (f(j+1)-f(j)) \frac{{\alpha}}{2d} \\ 
&= \sum\limits_{j={L}'}^{{U}'-1} \sqrt{\frac{\pi {\alpha}^2 (d-j)}{2e^4 j d^3}} (f(j+1)-f(j)) \notag\\ 
&\ge \sum\limits_{j={L}'}^{{U}'-1} \sqrt{\frac{\pi {\alpha}^2 (d-{U}')}{2e^4 {U}' d^3}} (f(j+1)-f(j)) \notag\\ 
&= \sqrt{\frac{\pi {\alpha}^2 (d-{U}')}{2e^4 {U}' d^3}} (f({U}')-f({L}')), \end{align}
where \eqref{eq:bound_int_4} follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:int_U_L} and ${\alpha} = \frac{1}{2} \min\left\{{U}'-{L}' , \sqrt{{L}'} , \sqrt{d - {U}'}\right\}$; \eqref{eq:bound_int_5} follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:stirling}.

nodes.name: Mean value theorem
Proof of Lemma 8
nodes.statement_short: If $q^*$ were extreme, $\hat\Gamma(q^*)$ would exceed the value Proposition 3 guarantees for some $q_0$, contradicting minimality.

nodes.name: Assume extreme q*
nodes.statement:
Suppose to the contrary that ${{q}^*} \in \left(0,\frac{1}{376017d^3}\right]\cup \left[1-\frac{1}{376017d^3},1\right)$. From \eqref{eq:convert_delta} we can bound 
\begin{align*}
    \frac{{{q}^*} }{1-{{q}^*}} \left({\Delta({{q}^*})}\right)^2&= \left( \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j (1-{{q}^*})^{d-j-1} ( f(j+1) - f(j) ) \right)^2 \cdot {{q}^*} (1-{{q}^*}) \notag \\
    &\leq\left( \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j (1-{{q}^*})^{d-j-1} \left( f(d) - f(0) \right) \right)^2 \cdot {{q}^*} (1-{{q}^*}) \notag \\
    & = (f(d) - f(0))^2 \cdot {{q}^*} (1-{{q}^*})\notag\\
    &\leq  (f(d) - f(0))^2 \times \frac{1}{376017d^3}\left(1-\frac{1}{376017d^3}\right) \notag \\ 
    &\le (f(d) - f(0))^2 \times \frac{1}{376017d^3}. 
\end{align*}
This along with the definition of ${\hat{\Gamma}} ({q})$ in \eqref{eq:def:fTp} yields that 
\begin{equation} {\hat{\Gamma}} ({{q}^*})  \geq 36.06 \times \frac{376017d^3}{ (f(d) - f(0))^2} \log \left( \frac{2n}{\varepsilon} \right).
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Contradiction
Proof of Lemma 9
nodes.statement:
For notational simplicity, let $\varsigma=\frac{1}{376017d^4}$. It follows from Lemma \ref{lem:q_range} that 
\begin{align}
    0<\frac {\varsigma}{{{q}^*}} < \frac{1}{d} \text{ and  }    0< \frac {\varsigma}{1-{{q}^*}} <  \frac{1}{d}.
\end{align}
For any ${\hat{{q}}^*} \in \left[ {{q}^*}-\varsigma , {{q}^*}+\varsigma \right]$, we have from \eqref{eq:convert_delta} that 
\begin{align}
    &\frac{{\hat{{q}}^*} }{1-{\hat{{q}}^*}}({\Delta({\hat{{q}}^*})})^2 \notag\\
    &= \left( \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {\hat{{q}}^*}^j (1-{\hat{{q}}^*})^{d-j-1} ( f(j+1) - f(j) ) \right)^2 \cdot {\hat{{q}}^*} (1-{\hat{{q}}^*}) \notag\\
    &\ge \left( \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} ({{q}^*}-\varsigma)^j (1-{{q}^*}-\varsigma)^{d-j-1} ( f(j+1) - f(j) ) \right)^2 \cdot ({{q}^*}-\varsigma) (1-{{q}^*}-\varsigma)  \notag\\
    &= \left( \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j\left(\frac{{{q}^*}-\varsigma}{{{q}^*}}\right)^j (1-{{q}^*})^{d-j-1}\left(\frac{1-{{q}^*}-\varsigma}{1-{{q}^*}}\right)^{d-j-1} ( f(j+1) - f(j) ) \right)^2 \cdot ({{q}^*}-\varsigma) (1-{\hat{{q}}^*}-\varsigma)  \notag\\
    &\geq \left( \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j\left(\frac{{{q}^*}-\varsigma}{{{q}^*}}\right)^{d-1} (1-{{q}^*})^{d-j-1}\left(\frac{1-{{q}^*}-\varsigma}{1-{{q}^*}}\right)^{d-1} ( f(j+1) - f(j) ) \right)^2 \cdot ({{q}^*}-\varsigma) (1-{\hat{{q}}^*}-\varsigma)  \notag\\
    &=\left( \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j (1-{{q}^*})^{d-j-1} ( f(j+1) - f(j) ) \right)^2 \cdot {{q}^*} (1-{{q}^*}) \cdot \left( \frac{{{q}^*}-\varsigma}{{{q}^*}} \right)^{2d-1} \left( \frac{1-{{q}^*}-\varsigma}{1-{{q}^*}} \right)^{2d-1} \notag\\
    &\ge \left( \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j (1-{{q}^*})^{d-j-1} ( f(j+1) - f(j) ) \right)^2 \cdot {{q}^*} (1-{{q}^*}) \cdot \left( 1 - \frac{1}{d} \right)^{2d-1} \left( 1 - \frac{1}{d} \right)^{2d-1} \notag\\ 
    &\ge \left( \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j (1-{{q}^*})^{d-j-1} ( f(j+1) - f(j) ) \right)^2 \times {{q}^*} (1-{{q}^*}) \times \frac{1}{8}\times \frac{1}{8} \notag\\ 
    &= \frac{1}{64} \times \frac{{{q}^*} ({\Delta({{q}^*})})^2}{1-{{q}^*}}. \end{align}
Using \eqref{eq:pgaph} along with the definition of ${\hat{\Gamma}} ({q})$ in \eqref{eq:def:fTp}, we have
\begin{align} {\hat{\Gamma}}({\hat{{q}}^*})\leq 64 {\hat{\Gamma}} ({{q}^*}).
\end{align}
For any ${\hat{{q}}^*} \in \left[ {{q}^*}-\varsigma , {{q}^*}+\varsigma \right]$, we also have 
\begin{align}
    {P(+,{\hat{{q}}^*})} &= \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {\hat{{q}}^*}^j (1-{\hat{{q}}^*})^{d-1-j} f(j+1) \notag\\ 
        &\leq  \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} ({{q}^*}+\varsigma)^j (1-{{q}^*}+\varsigma)^{d-1-j} f(j+1) \notag\\ 
        &\le \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j (1-{{q}^*})^{d-1-j} f(j+1) \cdot \left( \frac{{{q}^*}+\varsigma}{{{q}^*}} \right)^{d-1} \left( \frac{1-{{q}^*}+\varsigma}{1-{{q}^*}} \right)^{d-1} \notag\\ 
        &\le \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j (1-{{q}^*})^{d-1-j} f(j+1) \cdot \left( 1+\frac{1}{d} \right)^{d-1} \left( 1+\frac{1}{d} \right)^{d-1} \notag\\ 
        &\le \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j (1-{{q}^*})^{d-1-j} f(j+1) \cdot e^2 \notag \\ 
        &= e^2 {P(+,{{q}^*})}. \end{align}
And similarly,
\begin{align}
    1 - {Q(+,{\hat{{q}}^*})} &= \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {\hat{{q}}^*}^j (1-{\hat{{q}}^*})^{d-1-j} (1-f(j)) \notag\\ 
    &\le \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j (1-{{q}^*})^{d-1-j} (1-f(j)) \cdot \left( \frac{{{q}^*}+\varsigma}{{{q}^*}} \right)^{d-1} \left( \frac{1-{{q}^*}+\varsigma}{1-{{q}^*}} \right)^{d-1} \notag\\ 
    &\le \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j (1-{{q}^*})^{d-1-j} (1-f(j)) \cdot \left( 1+\frac{1}{d} \right)^{d-1} \left( 1+\frac{1}{d} \right)^{d-1} \notag\\ 
    &\le \sum\limits_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{d-1}{j} {{q}^*}^j (1-{{q}^*})^{d-1-j} (1-f(j)) \cdot e^2 \notag\\ 
    &= e^2 (1-{Q(+,{{q}^*})}). \end{align}
Combining \eqref{eq:pph} and \eqref{eq:ppmh}, along with the definition of ${P_{\min}({q})}$ in \eqref{eq:def:Pmin}, we have that 
\begin{equation} {P_{min}({\hat{{q}}^*})} \le e^2 P_{min}({{q}^*}).
\end{equation}
Finally, using \eqref{eq:Gammaprmie<=Gammap} and \eqref{eq:pminh} along with \eqref{eq:def:fTp} implies that 
\begin{equation*}
    {\Gamma({\hat{{q}}^*})}={\hat{\Gamma}}({\hat{{q}}^*}) {P_{min}({\hat{{q}}^*})}  \le 64 {\hat{\Gamma}} ({{q}^*}) e^2 P_{min}({{q}^*})=64e^2{\Gamma} ({{q}^*}),
\end{equation*}
which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Perturbing $q^*$ by $\varsigma$ changes $\hat\Gamma$ by at most a factor 64 and $P_{\min}$ by at most $e^2$.

Goal
nodes.statement: However, we will argue that ${\mathbb{E}} \left( \left(\frac{{i}-{\vartheta}}{{\gamma}({i})}\right)^2 \right) < 11$, which is a contradiction to \eqref{eq:mt:1st_conclusion}. This is proved for each of the two possible cases:

nodes.name: Case i condition
nodes.statement: ${\vartheta} \in (0,1)\cup (d-1,d)$;

nodes.name: Case ii condition
nodes.statement: ${\vartheta} \in[1, d-1]$.

nodes.name: Case i
nodes.statement:
Case \ref{eq:bound:exp:case1}: For ${\vartheta} \in (0,1)\cup (d-1,d)$, we have for any ${i} \in \{0,\dots, d\}$ that 
\begin{equation}
    \min\left\{ {i}+1 , d-{i}+1 \right\} \ge 1 > \min\{ {\vartheta} , d-{\vartheta} \}.
\end{equation}
It then follows that 
\begin{align} \left(\frac{{i}-{\vartheta}}{{\gamma}({i})}\right)^2 &= \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{\min \{ ({i} - {\vartheta})^2, {i}+1, d-{i}+1, {\vartheta}+1, d-{\vartheta}+1 \}} \notag\\
    &\le \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{\min \{ ({i} - {\vartheta})^2, {i}+1, d-{i}+1, {\vartheta}, d-{\vartheta} \}} \notag\\
    &= \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{\min \{ ({i} - {\vartheta})^2, {\vartheta}, d-{\vartheta} \}} \notag\\
    &\le \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{({i} - {\vartheta})^2} + \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{\min\{{\vartheta}, d-{\vartheta}\}} \notag\\
    &= 1 + \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2 \max\{{\vartheta}, d-{\vartheta}\}}{{\vartheta}(d-{\vartheta})} \notag\\
    &\le 1 + \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2 d}{{\vartheta}(d-{\vartheta})}.
\end{align}
Taking expectations on both sides of \eqref{eq:mt:value} w.r.t. the hypergeometric distribution \eqref{eq:hypergeometric:pdf}, we get
\begin{align} {\mathbb{E}} \left(  \left(\frac{{i}-{\vartheta}}{{\gamma}({i})}\right)^2 \right) &\le 1+ \frac{ d}{{\vartheta}(d-{\vartheta})}{\mathbb{E}} \left(({i}-{\vartheta})^2  \right).
\end{align}


From the mean formula in \eqref{eq:mean:var:formulae}, we have that 
${\mathbb{E}}({i})= {\chi}^{*} \frac d n ={\vartheta}$. 
Then using the variance formula in \eqref{eq:mean:var:formulae}, we have
\begin{align*}
    {\mathbb{E}} \left( ({i}-{\vartheta})^2\right) =  {\chi}^{*} \frac{d}{n}\cdot \frac{n-d}{n}\cdot \frac{n-{\chi}^{*}}{n-1},
\end{align*}
which implies 
 \begin{align} \frac{ d}{{\vartheta}(d-{\vartheta})}  {\mathbb{E}} \left( ({i}-{\vartheta})^2\right) =  \frac{n-d}{n-1} \leq 1.
\end{align}
Note that \eqref{eq:boundexp:comm} holds for all ${\vartheta}\in(0,d)$.
Substituting \eqref{eq:boundexp:comm} into \eqref{eq:boundexp:case1}, we have  ${\mathbb{E}} \left( \left(\frac{{i}-{\vartheta}}{{\gamma}({i})}\right)^2 \right) \leq 2$.

\begin{equation}
    \min\left\{ {i}+1 , d-{i}+1 \right\} \ge 1 > \min\{ {\vartheta} , d-{\vartheta} \}.
\end{equation}
It then follows that 
\begin{align} \left(\frac{{i}-{\vartheta}}{{\gamma}({i})}\right)^2 &= \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{\min \{ ({i} - {\vartheta})^2, {i}+1, d-{i}+1, {\vartheta}+1, d-{\vartheta}+1 \}} \notag\\
    &\le \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{\min \{ ({i} - {\vartheta})^2, {i}+1, d-{i}+1, {\vartheta}, d-{\vartheta} \}} \notag\\
    &= \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{\min \{ ({i} - {\vartheta})^2, {\vartheta}, d-{\vartheta} \}} \notag\\
    &\le \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{({i} - {\vartheta})^2} + \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{\min\{{\vartheta}, d-{\vartheta}\}} \notag\\
    &= 1 + \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2 \max\{{\vartheta}, d-{\vartheta}\}}{{\vartheta}(d-{\vartheta})} \notag\\
    &\le 1 + \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2 d}{{\vartheta}(d-{\vartheta})}.
\end{align}

nodes.name: Conclude Case i
nodes.statement: Substituting \eqref{eq:boundexp:comm} into \eqref{eq:boundexp:case1}, we have  ${\mathbb{E}} \left( \left(\frac{{i}-{\vartheta}}{{\gamma}({i})}\right)^2 \right) \leq 2$.

nodes.name: Case ii
nodes.statement:
Case \ref{eq:bound:exp:case2}: For ${\vartheta} \in[1, d-1]$, we must have $d \ge 2$. It follows that for any $i\in \{0, \dots, d\}$,    
\begin{align}
    \left(\frac{{i}-{\vartheta}}{{\gamma}({i})}\right)^2  &= \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{\min \{ ({i} - {\vartheta})^2, {i}+1, d-{i}+1, {\vartheta}+1, d-{\vartheta}+1 \}} \notag\\
    &\le \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{\min \{ ({i} - {\vartheta})^2, {i}+1, d-{i}+1, {\vartheta}, d-{\vartheta} \}} \notag\\
    &\le \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{({i} - {\vartheta})^2} + \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{\min \{ {i}+1, d-{i}+1 \}} + \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{\min\{{\vartheta}, d-{\vartheta}\}} \notag\\
    &= 1 + \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2 \max\{ {i}+1, d-{i}+1 \}}{({i}+1)(d-{i}+1)}+ \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2 \max\{{\vartheta}, d-{\vartheta}\}}{{\vartheta}(d-{\vartheta})}  \notag\\
    &\le 1  + \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2\left( d+1 \right)}{ ({i}+1) (d-{i}+1) } + \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2 d}{{\vartheta}(d-{\vartheta})}. \end{align}
Taking the expectation of \eqref{eq:mt:le_5} w.r.t. the hypergeometric distribution \eqref{eq:hypergeometric:pdf}, we have
\begin{align} {\mathbb{E}} \left(\left(\frac{{i}-{\vartheta}}{{\gamma}({i})}\right)^2\right) &\le 1 + \left( d+1 \right) {\mathbb{E}} \left( \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{({i}+1)(d-{i}+1)} \right) + \frac{ d}{{\vartheta}(d-{\vartheta})}{\mathbb{E}} \left(({i}-{\vartheta})^2  \right) \notag\\
    &\leq 2 + \left( d+1 \right) {\mathbb{E}} \left( \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{({i}+1)(d-{i}+1)} \right),

\end{align}
where the second line follows from \eqref{eq:boundexp:comm} since it continues to hold for this case. 



Next, we proceed to bound the term on the right hand side of \eqref{eq:mt:le:exp}.









We can expand
\begin{align}
    {\mathbb{E}} \left( \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{({i}+1)(d-{i}+1)} \right) 
    &= \sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d} \left( \frac{\binom{d}{{i}}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}-{i}}}{\binom{n}{{\chi}^{*}}} \cdot \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{({i}+1)(d-{i}+1)} \right) \notag\\
    &= \sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}+1}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot \frac{(n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)} \cdot ({i}-{\vartheta})^2 \right) \notag\\
    &= \frac{ (n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)} \cdot \sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}+1}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot ({i}-{\vartheta})^2 \right) \notag\\
    &\leq \frac{ (n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)} \cdot \sum \limits_{{i}=-1}^{d+1} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}+1}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot ({i}-{\vartheta})^2 \right) \notag\\
    &= \frac{ (n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)} \cdot \sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d+2} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}+1-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot ({i}-{\vartheta}-1)^2 \right). \end{align}
Using the formula for the mean of hypergeometric distributions $(n+2,d+2, {\chi}^{*}+1)$, we have 
$$\sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d+2} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}+1-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot {i} \right)=({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}.$$

Then, using the formula for the variance of hypergeometric distributions $(n+2,d+2, {\chi}^{*}+1)$, we have
\begin{align}  
\kern-2em \sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d+2} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}+1-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot ({i}-{\vartheta}-1)^2 \right) 
    &= \sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d+1} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}+1-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot \left( {i}-({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2} + ({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}-{\vartheta}-1 \right)^2 \right) \notag\\
 
    &= \sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d+1} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}+1-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot \left( {i}-({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}   \right)^2\right) + \left(({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}-{\vartheta}-1\right)^2\notag\\    
    &=  ({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}\cdot \frac{n-d}{n+2}\cdot \frac{n-{\chi}^{*}+1}{n+1} + \left(({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}-{\vartheta}-1\right)^2 \notag\\
    &\le ({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}\cdot \frac{n-d}{n+2}\cdot \frac{n-{\chi}^{*}+1}{n+1} + 4, \end{align}
where the last line follows from 
\begin{align*}
   0=  {\chi}^{*}\frac{d}{n}-{\vartheta} \leq  ({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}-{\vartheta} \leq ({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n}-{\vartheta} =\frac{d+2({\chi}^{*}+1)}{n}\leq 3.
\end{align*}
Substituting \eqref{eq:bound:var-case2} into \eqref{eq:exp-expand-case2}, we conclude that
\begin{align}
   {\mathbb{E}} \left( \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{({i}+1)(d-{i}+1)} \right)    
   &= \frac{1 }{d+1}\cdot \frac{n-d}{n+2}  + \frac{4 (n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)}\notag\\
   &\le \frac{1 }{d+1} +  \frac{4(n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)}\notag\\

    &\leq \frac{1 }{d+1} + \frac{4 }{d+1}\cdot \frac{n+2}{n+d}\cdot \frac{n+1}{n-\frac{n}{d}+1}\cdot \frac{d}{d+2} \notag\\
    &\le \frac{1 }{d+1} + \frac{4 }{d+1}\cdot  \frac{n+1}{n-\frac{n}{2}+1}\cdot \frac{nd+2d}{nd+2d+2n+d^2} \notag\\
    &< \frac{1 }{d+1} + \frac{4 }{d+1} \times 2 \times 1 \notag\\
    &= \frac{9}{d+1}, \end{align}
where the third line follows from 
\begin{align*}
    ({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)&=-\left({\chi}^{*}-\frac{n}{2}\right)^2+\frac{n^2}{4}+n+1\\ &\geq-\left(\frac{n}{d}-\frac{n}{2}\right)^2+\frac{n^2}{4}+n+1 \\
    &=\left(\frac{n}{d}+1\right)\left(n-\frac{n}{d}+1\right)
\end{align*}
since we have from \eqref{eq:def:vartheta} that $\frac{n}{d}\leq {\chi}^{*}\leq n-\frac{n}{d}$ for $ 1\leq {\vartheta} \leq d-1$.
Upon combining \eqref{eq:mt:le:exp} and \eqref{eq:mt:le_3_9}, we arrive at
\begin{align*}
    {\mathbb{E}} \left(\frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{ {\gamma}({i})^2}\right)
    < 2 + \left( d+1 \right) \cdot \frac{9}{d+1} = 11.
\end{align*}

    &= \frac{ (n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)} \cdot \sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}+1}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot ({i}-{\vartheta})^2 \right) \notag\\
    &\leq \frac{ (n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)} \cdot \sum \limits_{{i}=-1}^{d+1} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}+1}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot ({i}-{\vartheta})^2 \right) \notag\\
    &= \frac{ (n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)} \cdot \sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d+2} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}+1-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot ({i}-{\vartheta}-1)^2 \right).
nodes.label: eq:exp-expand-case2

nodes.name: Second moment
Equation (198)
nodes.statement:
\kern-2em \sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d+2} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}+1-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot ({i}-{\vartheta}-1)^2 \right) 
    &= \sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d+1} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}+1-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot \left( {i}-({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2} + ({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}-{\vartheta}-1 \right)^2 \right) \notag\\
 
    &= \sum \limits_{{i}=0}^{d+1} \left( \frac{\binom{d+2}{{i}}\binom{n-d}{{\chi}^{*}+1-{i}}}{\binom{n+2}{{\chi}^{*}+1}} \cdot \left( {i}-({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}   \right)^2\right) + \left(({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}-{\vartheta}-1\right)^2\notag\\    
    &=  ({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}\cdot \frac{n-d}{n+2}\cdot \frac{n-{\chi}^{*}+1}{n+1} + \left(({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}-{\vartheta}-1\right)^2 \notag\\
    &\le ({\chi}^{*}+1)\frac{d+2}{n+2}\cdot \frac{n-d}{n+2}\cdot \frac{n-{\chi}^{*}+1}{n+1} + 4,
nodes.label: eq:bound:var-case2

nodes.name: Bound by 9/(d+1)
nodes.statement:
Substituting \eqref{eq:bound:var-case2} into \eqref{eq:exp-expand-case2}, we conclude that
\begin{align}
   {\mathbb{E}} \left( \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{({i}+1)(d-{i}+1)} \right)    
   &= \frac{1 }{d+1}\cdot \frac{n-d}{n+2}  + \frac{4 (n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)}\notag\\
   &\le \frac{1 }{d+1} +  \frac{4(n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)}\notag\\

    &\leq \frac{1 }{d+1} + \frac{4 }{d+1}\cdot \frac{n+2}{n+d}\cdot \frac{n+1}{n-\frac{n}{d}+1}\cdot \frac{d}{d+2} \notag\\
    &\le \frac{1 }{d+1} + \frac{4 }{d+1}\cdot  \frac{n+1}{n-\frac{n}{2}+1}\cdot \frac{nd+2d}{nd+2d+2n+d^2} \notag\\
    &< \frac{1 }{d+1} + \frac{4 }{d+1} \times 2 \times 1 \notag\\
    &= \frac{9}{d+1}, \end{align}
where the third line follows from 
\begin{align*}
    ({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)&=-\left({\chi}^{*}-\frac{n}{2}\right)^2+\frac{n^2}{4}+n+1\\ &\geq-\left(\frac{n}{d}-\frac{n}{2}\right)^2+\frac{n^2}{4}+n+1 \\
    &=\left(\frac{n}{d}+1\right)\left(n-\frac{n}{d}+1\right)
\end{align*}
since we have from \eqref{eq:def:vartheta} that $\frac{n}{d}\leq {\chi}^{*}\leq n-\frac{n}{d}$ for $ 1\leq {\vartheta} \leq d-1$.

nodes.name: Equation (199)
nodes.statement:
{\mathbb{E}} \left( \frac{({i}-{\vartheta})^2}{({i}+1)(d-{i}+1)} \right)    
   &= \frac{1 }{d+1}\cdot \frac{n-d}{n+2}  + \frac{4 (n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)}\notag\\
   &\le \frac{1 }{d+1} +  \frac{4(n+1)(n+2)}{({\chi}^{*}+1)(n-{\chi}^{*}+1)(d+1)(d+2)}\notag\\

    &\leq \frac{1 }{d+1} + \frac{4 }{d+1}\cdot \frac{n+2}{n+d}\cdot \frac{n+1}{n-\frac{n}{d}+1}\cdot \frac{d}{d+2} \notag\\
    &\le \frac{1 }{d+1} + \frac{4 }{d+1}\cdot  \frac{n+1}{n-\frac{n}{2}+1}\cdot \frac{nd+2d}{nd+2d+2n+d^2} \notag\\
    &< \frac{1 }{d+1} + \frac{4 }{d+1} \times 2 \times 1 \notag\\
    &= \frac{9}{d+1},
nodes.label: eq:mt:le_3_9

nodes.name: Conclude Case ii
Conclusion
nodes.statement:
Summarizing the above two cases, we see that ${\mathbb{E}} \left( \left(\frac{{i}-{\vartheta}}{{\gamma}({i})}\right)^2 \right) < 11$,
which contradicts \eqref{eq:mt:1st_conclusion}. Therefore, the assumption in \eqref{eq:mt:cv_aspt_previous} is false and Lemma~\ref{lem:match} is proved.

On the other hand,  recall from Remark \ref{remark:lb} that the lower bound in \eqref{eq:T:lower:bound} scales as $\Omega\left(\log \binom{n}{d}\right)$.\footnote{By a similar argument to the one above, one can show the lower bound is precisely $\log \binom{n}{d}$, i.e., we also have ${h(f)}=1$ for this test function.}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 20
nodes.statement:
Let ${{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}$ denote the probability of having a positive test outcome conditioned on $d={\hat{d}}-1$. It follows that
\begin{equation*} 
    {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})} = \sum\limits_{j=0}^{{\hat{d}}-1} \binom{{\hat{d}}-1}{j} {\zeta}^j (1-{\zeta})^{{\hat{d}}-1-j} f(j).
\end{equation*}
Then we have
    \begin{align}
        {{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} - {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})} &= \sum\limits_{j=0}^{{\hat{d}}} \binom{{\hat{d}}}{j} {\zeta}^j (1-{\zeta})^{{\hat{d}}-j} f(j) - \sum\limits_{j=0}^{{\hat{d}}-1} \binom{{\hat{d}}-1}{j} {\zeta}^j (1-{\zeta})^{{\hat{d}}-1-j} f(j) \notag\\
        &= (1-{\zeta}) \sum\limits_{j=0}^{{\hat{d}}} \left( \binom{{\hat{d}}-1}{j} + \binom{{\hat{d}}-1}{j-1} \right) {\zeta}^j (1-{\zeta})^{{\hat{d}}-1-j} f(j) - \sum\limits_{j=0}^{{\hat{d}}-1} \binom{{\hat{d}}-1}{j} {\zeta}^j (1-{\zeta})^{{\hat{d}}-1-j} f(j) \notag\\
        &= (1-{\zeta}) \sum\limits_{j=1}^{{\hat{d}}} \binom{{\hat{d}}-1}{j-1} {\zeta}^j (1-{\zeta})^{{\hat{d}}-1-j} f(j) - {\zeta} \sum\limits_{j=0}^{{\hat{d}}-1} \binom{{\hat{d}}-1}{j} {\zeta}^j (1-{\zeta})^{{\hat{d}}-1-j} f(j) \notag\\
        &= {\zeta} \sum\limits_{j=1}^{{\hat{d}}} \binom{{\hat{d}}-1}{j-1} {\zeta}^{j-1} (1-{\zeta})^{{\hat{d}}-j} f(j) - {\zeta} \sum\limits_{j=0}^{{\hat{d}}-1} \binom{{\hat{d}}-1}{j} {\zeta}^j (1-{\zeta})^{{\hat{d}}-1-j} f(j) \notag\\
        &= {\zeta} \sum\limits_{j=0}^{{\hat{d}}-1} \binom{{\hat{d}}-1}{j} {\zeta}^j (1-{\zeta})^{{\hat{d}}-1-j} (f(j+1) - f(j)) \notag\\
        &= \frac{{\zeta}}{1-{\zeta}} {\Delta({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}. \end{align}
    Using this observation, the threshold equation \eqref{eq:lom_l} is equivalent to
    \begin{equation} \frac{{t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}}{{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}} \le \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2}.
    \end{equation}
    For ${\texttt{LoM}}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})$ two types of error can happen:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\roman*)]
    \item We have $d \le {\hat{d}}-1$, but is claimed to be $d \ge {\hat{d}}$; \item We have $d \ge {\hat{d}}$, but is claimed to be $d \le {\hat{d}}-1$. \end{enumerate}

    Case \ref{sub:error:TypeI}: It is worth noting that ${t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \sim \text{Binomial} \left({t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} , {{P}(d,{\zeta})}\right)$. From \eqref{eq:sub:threshold} we know the probability of error is
    \begin{align*}
        \Pr \left( \frac{{t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}}{{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}} > \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2} \right) &= \Pr \left( {t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} > \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2}\cdot{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \right)\\
        &\le \Pr \left( \text{Binomial} \left({t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} , {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}\right) > \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2} \cdot {t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \right) \\
        &\le \exp \left( -\frac{1}{3} \left( \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}-{{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2{{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}} \right)^2 \cdot{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}\right) \\
        
        &\le \exp \left( - \frac{\left({{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}-{{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}\right)^2}{12} {t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \right) \\
        &\leq {\epsilon}.
    \end{align*}
       where the first inequality follows from the fact that ${{P}(d,{\zeta})}$ is monotonically increasing with respect to $d$ and $d \leq {\hat{d}}-1$; the second inequality follows from Chernoff bound in Fact \ref{chernoff_bound}; the third inequality follows from the fact that ${{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}\leq 1$; the last inequality follows by substituting \eqref{eq:def:lomrs} and \eqref{eq:lompgap_dif}.


    Case \ref{sub:error:TypeII}: The calculations are similar to Case \ref{sub:error:TypeI}. Once again,  ${t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \sim \text{Binomial} \left({t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} , {{P}(d,{\zeta})}\right)$. We know from \eqref{eq:sub:threshold} that the probability of error is
    \begin{align*}
        \Pr \left( \frac{{t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}}{{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}} \le \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2} \right) &= \Pr \left( {t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \le \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2}\cdot{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \right)\\
        &\le \Pr \left( \text{Binomial} \left({t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} , {{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}\right) \le \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2} \cdot {t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \right) \\
        &\le \exp \left( -\frac{1}{3} \left( \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}-{{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}} \right)^2 \cdot{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} {{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}\right) \\
        
        &\le \exp \left( - \frac{\left({{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}-{{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}\right)^2}{12} {t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \right) \\
        &\leq {\epsilon}.
    \end{align*}
     where the first inequality follows from the fact that ${{P}(d,{\zeta})}$ is monotonically increasing with respect to $d$ and $d \ge {\hat{d}}$; the second inequality follows from Chernoff bound in Fact \ref{chernoff_bound}; the third inequality follow from the fact that ${{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}\leq 1$; the last inequality follows by substituting \eqref{eq:def:lomrs} and \eqref{eq:lompgap_dif}.


    Combining the two cases we conclude that the error probability of ${\texttt{LoM}}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})$  is at most ${\epsilon}$.

Case \ref{sub:error:TypeI}: It is worth noting that ${t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \sim \text{Binomial} \left({t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} , {{P}(d,{\zeta})}\right)$. From \eqref{eq:sub:threshold} we know the probability of error is
    \begin{align*}
        \Pr \left( \frac{{t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}}{{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}} > \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2} \right) &= \Pr \left( {t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} > \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2}\cdot{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \right)\\
        &\le \Pr \left( \text{Binomial} \left({t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} , {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}\right) > \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2} \cdot {t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \right) \\
        &\le \exp \left( -\frac{1}{3} \left( \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}-{{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2{{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}} \right)^2 \cdot{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}\right) \\
        
        &\le \exp \left( - \frac{\left({{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}-{{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}\right)^2}{12} {t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \right) \\
        &\leq {\epsilon}.
    \end{align*}
       where the first inequality follows from the fact that ${{P}(d,{\zeta})}$ is monotonically increasing with respect to $d$ and $d \leq {\hat{d}}-1$; the second inequality follows from Chernoff bound in Fact \ref{chernoff_bound}; the third inequality follows from the fact that ${{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}\leq 1$; the last inequality follows by substituting \eqref{eq:def:lomrs} and \eqref{eq:lompgap_dif}.
nodes.statement_short: Type I error at most $\epsilon$ by Chernoff.

nodes.name: Case II
nodes.statement:
Case \ref{sub:error:TypeII}: The calculations are similar to Case \ref{sub:error:TypeI}. Once again,  ${t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \sim \text{Binomial} \left({t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} , {{P}(d,{\zeta})}\right)$. We know from \eqref{eq:sub:threshold} that the probability of error is
    \begin{align*}
        \Pr \left( \frac{{t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}}{{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}} \le \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2} \right) &= \Pr \left( {t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \le \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2}\cdot{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \right)\\
        &\le \Pr \left( \text{Binomial} \left({t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} , {{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}\right) \le \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} + {{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2} \cdot {t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \right) \\
        &\le \exp \left( -\frac{1}{3} \left( \frac{{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}-{{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}}{2{{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}} \right)^2 \cdot{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} {{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}\right) \\
        
        &\le \exp \left( - \frac{\left({{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}-{{P}({\hat{d}}-1,{\zeta})}\right)^2}{12} {t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})} \right) \\
        &\leq {\epsilon}.
    \end{align*}
     where the first inequality follows from the fact that ${{P}(d,{\zeta})}$ is monotonically increasing with respect to $d$ and $d \ge {\hat{d}}$; the second inequality follows from Chernoff bound in Fact \ref{chernoff_bound}; the third inequality follow from the fact that ${{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}\leq 1$; the last inequality follows by substituting \eqref{eq:def:lomrs} and \eqref{eq:lompgap_dif}.
nodes.statement_short: Type II error at most $\epsilon$ by Chernoff.

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: Combining the two cases we conclude that the error probability of ${\texttt{LoM}}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})$  is at most ${\epsilon}$.

nodes.name: Full algorithm
nodes.statement:
Armed with the above subroutine ${\texttt{LoM}}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})$, the algorithm for exactly estimating $d$ is now described in Algorithm \ref{algo:est}. 
\begin{algorithm}
    \caption{Exact estimation of $d$} \begin{algorithmic}[1]
    \State $\textbf{Initialize } {\epsilon} \gets \frac{{\varepsilon}}{2\log n + 2}$, ${d_u} \gets 2$
    \While{true}
        \State $\textbf{set } {{\zeta}^*} = \mathrm{argmin}_{{\zeta}\in(0,1)} \frac{1-{\zeta}}{{\zeta} ({\Delta({d_u},{\zeta})})^2}$
        \State $\textbf{run } {\texttt{LoM}}({d_u},{{\zeta}^*},{\epsilon})$
        \State $\textbf{if } d \le {d_u}-1 \textbf{ then halt}$
        \State $\textbf{else set } {d_u} \gets 2{d_u}$
    \EndWhile
    \State $\textbf{set } {d_l} \gets \frac{{d_u}}{2}$

    \While{${d_u} - {d_l} \ge 2$}
        \State $\textbf{set } {d_m} = \left\lfloor \frac{{d_l}+{d_u}}{2} \right\rfloor \text{, } {{\zeta}^*} = \mathrm{argmin}_{{\zeta}\in(0,1)} \frac{1-{\zeta}}{{\zeta} ({\Delta({d_m},{\zeta})})^2}$
        \State $\textbf{run } {\texttt{LoM}}({d_m},{{\zeta}^*},{\epsilon})$
        \State $\textbf{if } d \le {d_m}-1 \textbf{ then set } {d_u} \gets {d_m}$
        \State $\textbf{else set } {d_l} \gets {d_m}$
    \EndWhile
    \State $\textbf{output } {d_l}$
    \end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}






We start by noting that both while loops in Algorithm \ref{algo:est} invoke at most $\log (2d)$ calls to the subroutine ${\texttt{LoM}}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})$. By Lemma \ref{lem:sub:error} and the union bound, we know that the error probability of Algorithm \ref{algo:est} is bounded from above by $$2 \log (2d) \cdot {\epsilon} =2 \log (2d)\frac{{\varepsilon}}{2\log n + 2}\le {\varepsilon}.$$


From \eqref{eq:def:lomrs} we have
\begin{align*}
    {t({\hat{d}},{{\zeta}^*},{\epsilon})} &= \left\lceil 8.32 \left( \frac{1-{{\zeta}^*}}{{{\zeta}^*} {\Delta({\hat{d}},{{\zeta}^*})}} \right)^2 \log \frac{1}{{\epsilon}}  \right\rceil\\
    &\le \left\lceil 8.32 \left( \frac{1-{{\zeta}^*}}{{{\zeta}^*} ({\Delta({\hat{d}},{{\zeta}^*})})^2} \right)^2 \log \frac{1}{{\epsilon}} \right\rceil\\
    &\le 8.32 \left(376017 H(f,{\hat{d}}) \, {\hat{d}}\right)^2\log \frac{1}{{\epsilon}}+1  \\
    &= 8.32 \left(376017 H(f,{\hat{d}}) \, {\hat{d}} \right)^2 \log\left(\frac{2\log n+2} { {\varepsilon} }\right)+1.
\end{align*}
The first inequality follows by noting that ${\Delta({\hat{d}},{{\zeta}^*})}\leq 1$ since ${\Delta({\hat{d}},{\zeta})}$ in \eqref{eq:def:lompgap} is the same as ${\Delta({q})}$ in \eqref{eq:convert_delta} (with $({\hat{d}},{{\zeta}^*})$ in place of $(d,{q})$), and ${\Delta({q})}\leq 1 $ for all ${q}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:relation:quantities}. The second inequality can be justified as follows: The expression in $(\cdot)^2$ is similar to ${\hat{\Gamma}} ({q})$ in \eqref{eq:def:fTp}. By the same argument as in Proposition \ref{prop:existence_final} and the discussions that follow, we can bound the expression in $(\cdot)^2$ by $376017 H(f,{\hat{d}}) \, {\hat{d}}$, where $H(f,{\hat{d}})$ is the same as ${H(f)}$ in \eqref{eq:def:sensi:para} but with ${\hat{d}} $ in place of $d$.


Lastly, since ${\texttt{LoM}}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})$ is called ${\cal O}(\log d)$ times and ${\hat{d}}\in{\cal O}(d) $, the above inequality implies that the total number of tests in Algorithm \ref{algo:est} scales as ${\cal O} \left(\left({H(f)} d\right)^2 \log d \log\left(\frac{\log n}{{\varepsilon} }\right)\right)$. This completes the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:estimation:d}.

nodes.name: Threshold test
nodes.statement:
Let ${t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}$ denote the number of tests with positive outcome within these ${t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}$ tests. If
    \begin{equation} \frac{{t^{+}({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}}{{t({\hat{d}},{\zeta},{\epsilon})}} \le {{P}({\hat{d}},{\zeta})} - \frac{{\zeta}}{2(1-{\zeta})} {\Delta({\hat{d}},{\zeta})},
    \end{equation}
    return  $d \le {\hat{d}}-1$; otherwise, return $d \ge {\hat{d}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare the positive fraction with $P(\hat d,\zeta)-\frac{\zeta}{2(1-\zeta)}\Delta(\hat d,\zeta)$ and return the decision.
